complexity.notes: Correct but redundant: maxDepth is recomputed for every subtree. A bottom-up pass returning (height, balanced) pairs or a sentinel like -1 achieves O(n) time. Also, generalized inputs deeper than CPython's recursion limit (~1000) would hit RecursionError, though the stated cap of 1000 nodes makes this a non-issue here.
complexity.summary: Top-down check: at every node it recomputes the heights of both subtrees with a separate maxDepth traversal and compares them, recursing into children. On a balanced tree each level's heights cost O(n) total giving O(n log n), but on a degenerate (chain) tree the repeated height computations sum to O(n^2).
